ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 6516, as amended through 2024, Arts. 2, 5-4, 7) and its Enforcement Decree (Presidential Decree No. 27093, as amended); Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality Act (Act No. 5493, as amended); Korean Commercial Act (Act No. 1000, as amended, Arts. 287-2 to 287-74 for Yuhan Hoesa); Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 5559, as amended); and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) examination and reporting regulations.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Company Registry Certificate, certified excerpt)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent District Court Registry Office, Supreme Court of Korea, or competent companies registrar of the document's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing country is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention: notarize the underlying foreign instrument, submit it to that country's designated Competent Authority for Apostille, and attach a notarized English/Korean translation; do NOT add consular legalization. If the issuing country is not an Apostille Convention member: notarization -> authentication by the country's Ministry of Foreign Affairs -> legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate; apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Corporate Existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Supreme Court Registry Office / foreign state corporate registrar
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path for Convention member states, or consular legalization path for non-member states, in accordance with the same parallel and mutually exclusive sequence described above.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney appointing the Korean incorporation agent and local representative director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate board of the foreign parent/shareholder, notarized in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local notary, followed by Apostille (Hague Convention member) or by Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and Korean consular legalization (non-member state). Never both.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Memorandum of Association / Yuhan Hoesa Deed)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean law firm drafting attorney or foreign parent's notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For foreign-sourced signatures and corporate approvals: Apostille/consular legalization as a mutually exclusive authentication branch; Korean Articles of Association must also be notarized in Korean and filed with the registry court.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the foreign parent's or shareholder's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent shareholder's commercial bank, subject to that bank's signatory and notarization rules
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank signature certification -> Apostille (Convention state) OR Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication -> Korean Embassy/Consulate legalization (non-Convention state). The two paths are mutually exclusive and must not be cumulated.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, ultimate beneficial owners, authorized signatories and counterparties against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC sdn list, Korean Financial Action Task Force/KoFIU consolidated financial sanctions list, the Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act embargo designations, and domestic criminal-records checks. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, with senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Any match, close alternative, or anomalous wire under Swift/TT payment rails triggers a Suspicious Transaction Report to KoFIU and a legal hold.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (i-Plus) and the competent district court registry window
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Yuhan Hoesa trade name must be registered in Korean (Hangul). The name must include the mandatory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa. The four-tier convention requires (1) an individualizing element, (2) a business-object descriptor consistent with the registered scope, (3) the legal-form element Yuhan Hoesa, and (4) an optional English transliteration for trade use only outside the Korean statutory register. Chinese characters or other scripts are not accepted as the registered Korean corporate name; non-Korean names must be transliterated into Hangul phonetically. English names may appear in parent resolutions and contracts but not as the registered corporate name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the registry court will issue a written reason specifying the conflicting registered trademark, prohibited word, or identity-confusing name. The applicant or its Korean attorney must, within 14 days of service, file a written rectification request with the registry head or a formal appeal under the Commercial Registration Rules; an immediate appeal to the appellate district court is available within two weeks. If rejection is based on a sensitive token requiring ministerial approval (e.g. Bank), the applicant must first obtain the relevant financial regulator's non-objection or permit. If the minister denies approval, the applicant may institute administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act within 90 days. A fresh name-reservation application may be submitted once the conflicting mark or token is removed or authorized.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a wholesale distributor of clinical diagnostic ELISA assays and IVD reagents, a pure virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding address is not operationally permissible. The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) license for IVD reagent wholesaling requires a physical place of business, storage facilities meeting reagent storage/temperature standards, and a responsible licensee; municipal tax authorities under the Local Tax Act and VAT registration practice also require actual business-premises presence. Banks will reject a virtual-office address at KYC/account-opening. A serviced office, officetel, or shared laboratory facility with a real desk, telephone line, accessible records, and compliant cold-chain storage may satisfy the registration and licensing reviewer.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Unannounced physical inspection risk for this distribution business is High within the first 12 months (estimated 65-75%) for MFDS license compliance, and Medium (approximately 25-30%) for municipal tax/registry checks. Checklist: visible company signage; availability of leased office/storage contracts; temperature-monitored reagent storage and cold-chain records; statutory books and registry filings on site; employment records and social-insurance enrollment; shipping/receiving logs; VAT invoices and bank account statements; director/employee access to the premises; and response readiness within the registry's statutory inspection notification window.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Part/Chapter on Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), Articles 287-2 through 287-74; Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 4 through 6; Registration of Real Estate and Corporation Registration Act; Electronic Court Registration Procedures Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporate Registration Division of the competent Local District Court (including the Seoul Central District Court) acting under the Court Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea; for foreign investors, KOTRA Invest Korea and designated foreign exchange banks.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation Registration of a Yuhan Hoesa (Limited Liability Company), together with the Notarized Articles of Incorporation, Capital Deposit Certificate, Foreign Investment Notice certificate, and statutory officer consent and specimen signature forms.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is required for a South Korean Yuhan Hoesa under the Commercial Act. There is no mandatory blocked escrow account. However, the initial share capital must be fully paid into a temporary capital deposit bank account before the court registration, and a bank capital deposit certificate must be filed with the court. If the foreign investor needs foreign investment status under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the investment amount must satisfy the statutory reporting threshold of KRW 100,000,000, but this threshold is not a general paid-in capital formation minimum.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY) WHEREAS, the incorporators of Yuhan Hoesa (the Company) have established the Company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea and have prepared notarized Articles of Incorporation; WHEREAS, the directors of the Company have been duly appointed and form the initial Board of Directors; WHEREAS, the Company needs to ratify the subscription of share capital, open bank accounts, fix its registered office, and appoint statutory officers so as to carry on the wholesale distribution of clinical diagnostic ELISA assays and reagents under ISIC 4649; WHEREAS, the Board is authorized to take all actions necessary to complete incorporation, licensing, and operational startup of the Company. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that: 1. The authorized and subscribed share capital of the Company, as set out in the Articles of Incorporation and the subscription statement, is hereby ratified. The representative director is directed to collect all initial capital contributions, cause the same to be deposited in the Company's capital deposit account, obtain the bank's capital deposit certificate, and file the same with the local district court at incorporation registration. 2. The registered office of the Company shall be, and is, fixed at the address described in the Articles of Incorporation. The representative director and any director are authorized to execute the lease agreement, register the office with the local district court, and file address changes with the National Tax Service and all licensing authorities. 3. A commercial bank account of the Company shall be opened at a bank selected by the Company. The bank is authorized to accept SWIFT, wire, and telegraphic transfer payments for capital and trade purposes. For each account, the bank shall act in accordance with the account mandate, with transactions exceeding KRW 100,000,000 requiring two joint signatures; all transactions must comply with Korean AML/CFT regulations. 4. Each of the following persons is appointed to the office set opposite their name: [CEO and Representative Director]; [Director of Finance]; [Director of Compliance]; [Statutory Auditor]. Each statutory officer shall hold office until the first annual general meeting of members or until a successor is appointed, and is vested with authority to represent, sign, and bind the Company within the scope of law. 5. The directors and officers are authorized to prepare, execute, deliver and file

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: Home Tax (Hometax) system available at https://www.hometax.go.kr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity conducting taxable business in Korea, registration is mandatory. Step 1: Confirm the existence of a Korean place of business; if none, appoint a domestic tax representative under Article 82 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. Step 2: Prepare the corporate formation dossier, including certificate of incorporation and articles of association (with apostille/consular legalization), board resolution appointing the local officer or tax representative, power of attorney, and passport copies of authorized signatories. Step 3: File the business registration application (Business Registration Form) with the competent NTS district tax office (or the Seoul Regional Tax Office for foreign entities without a domestic permanent establishment), either online via the Hometax portal or in person at the tax office. Step 4: Obtain the 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which functions as the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT ID. Step 5: Register for electronic tax invoice issuance on Hometax and procure the authorized digital certificate required for e-invoicing and secure VAT filings. The BRN remains effective for all corporate income tax, VAT, and withholding tax compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No generic check-the-box election is available under Korean tax law. A statutory group consolidation election exists under Article 43-2 of the Corporate Tax Act for a domestic parent company that owns 100% of one or more wholly-owned domestic subsidiaries. No hybrid mismatch elections are available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None - VAT registration is mandatory from the date of commencing any taxable business activity in Korea; there is no monetary exemption threshold for foreign non-resident entities. For domestic micro-enterprises, a simplified taxpayer scheme applies on annual turnover below KRW 80,000,000, but registration is still required.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic tax invoices (ETIs) through the NTS Hometax platform. Detailed supply data must be transmitted to the NTS within one business day after the supply. Real-time validation, anti-fraud analytics, and digital signature authentication (using an authorized public certificate) are mandated. ERP/API integration is supported. Violations of electronic invoicing obligations attract penalty taxes and rejection of input VAT deductions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated VAT (0%) applies to the export of tangible goods under Article 21 of the VAT Act, including wholesale distribution of clinical diagnostic ELISA assays and reagents, provided the goods are definitively exported from Korea to a foreign destination. Qualifying offshore digital services or export-related services may also be zero-rated. The exporter must maintain contemporaneous documentation demonstrating physical export and receive the export proceeds in foreign currency within the statutory repatriation window.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration (Electronic Export Declaration Receipt / Export Declaration Confirmation)
Commercial Bill of Lading (or Airway Bill) evidencing physical movement from Korea to the foreign destination
Foreign Exchange Bank transaction statement / Certificate of Export Proceeds (equivalent to an Inward Remittance Certificate) evidencing foreign currency receipt
KCS EDI export clearance report and customs broker confirmation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent or unsubstantiated export zero-rating claims are subject to retrospective VAT assessment at the standard 10% rate, plus additional tax charges under Article 60 of the VAT Act (up to 40% for intentional misdeclaration and 10% for negligent understatement) plus daily late-payment surcharges. Criminal penalties may be imposed under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act, including imprisonment and fines for tax evasion. Customs violations may trigger additional penalties under the Customs Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, and any refunded VAT amount is clawed back with accrued interest. The NTS may also invalidate the relevant e-tax invoices, disallow input VAT credits, and pursue criminal referrals for serious offenses.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK) as the central monetary authority, operating in tandem with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) through the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, delegated to the Foreign Exchange Information System and the Korea Customs Service for trade settlement monitoring
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a free-floating exchange rate regime under a broad current and capital account liberalization framework. The Korean won (KRW) is fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in goods and services, profit remittances, dividends, and royalties, subject to filing and verification through designated foreign exchange banks. Capital account transactions require a more formal reporting or licensing framework; while portfolio investment and inbound equity ownership are largely open, resident and non-resident entities must route transactions through a domestic foreign exchange bank and within the prescribed purpose codes. Surrender requirements are no longer a blanket mandatory conversion rule; however, exporters must convert FD or KRW proceeds within a settlement period under a 'received foreign exchange holding' system unless a deferral or exemption is granted by the bank. Profit remittance hurdles are predominantly documentary: audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, pay-in evidence of subscribed paid-in capital, and a draft remittance application under purpose code C-I-1 (dividend distribution). In practice, the capital verification requirement of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act for foreign-invested enterprises requires a certificate of completion of external capital introduction before any outbound capital transfer. The overall convertibility is characterized as high, but the reverse regulatory requirement to repatriate export proceeds within a designated time horizon, and the need to obtain advance notification for aggregate cross-border borrowings above KRW 30 billion equivalent, constitute nuanced operational frictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Bank of Korea's Foreign Exchange Operation Regulations, exporters must sell or convert export foreign currency receipts into KRW within the settlement due date, generally the foreign exchange receipt date plus a statutory tolerance of 30 calendar days, unless the exporter has applied for and received an extension or qualifies for an exemption under the 'export proceeds reinvestment' or 'offshore trade receivables offset' provisions. The mandatory conversion ratio is effectively 100% of the export proceeds received in foreign currency, as Korean law requires the repatriation and settlement of trade receivables in Korea unless a specific exemption is granted. For a distributor of diagnostic reagents, the invoice currency may be USD but the equivalent KRW must be accounted for and the trade settlement through a domestic bank is mandatory, with proof of settlement submitted for export tax rebate and customs clearance.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/USD multi-currency)
Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW/JPY/USD)
Basic Operational Currency Account and Export Proceeds Settlement Account
Basic Operational Currency Account and Foreign Currency Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital electronic money institutions and neobanks have a legally constrained viability in South Korea. Any financial services entity, including a transfer-only EMI, must obtain a license under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act or be registered as a small-amount electronic payment service provider with the Financial Services Commission. A non-resident overseas EMI, particularly one operating solely through a remote account opening interface without a physical Korean branch, is legally barred from maintaining a domestic won settlement account or holding a foreign exchange business license. Consequently, offshore EMIs cannot be used as primary treasury rails for a Korean corporation; they may only act as a supplementary document repository or source of reference, never as the regulated clearing bank. The recommended treasury route is through a domestic Tier-1 commercial bank acting as the designated foreign exchange bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company), the statutory director and the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) must appear in-person at the bank branch in South Korea to complete corporate account opening, unless the bank permits a remote cross-border video interview under its 'remote customer identification' procedure approved by the Financial Services Commission, which is very rare and only available for existing trusted clients. For newcomers, a physical presence of the director (or a power-of-attorney holder accompanied by a certified apostilled corporate resolution) is mandated for the first account activation. All corporate signatories must present original certificates of corporate seal (corporate registration certificate), business registration certificate, and directors' personal IDs. The capital escrow account used for the statutory foreign investment declaration requires the physical presence of the foreign investor or a designated local attorney with notarized and apostilled authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between declared business scope (wholesale distribution of IVD diagnostic reagents) and the actual physical import/export records, triggering a false-invoice or trade-based money laundering red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full customs clearance dataset (ELMAS and UNI-PASS export declarations), signed commercial contracts with the end-hospital or distributor, quarantine and storage certificates for cold-chain reagents, ISO 13485 quality certificates, and a three-month vendor package from the overseas manufacturer listing batch numbers and shipping dates, all notarized and matching the invoice amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or shareholder has been flagged on discrete sanctions screening, possibly due to common-name matching with a politically exposed person or a suspicious transaction report from another jurisdiction, causing an automatic enhanced due diligence referral.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a comprehensive negative media report from a reputable corporate intelligence service, certified copies of passports and national IDs with clear nationality, source-of-wealth evidence (tax returns, bank statements, dividend records) covering the last 24 months, an explanatory statement regarding any same-name matches, and a commitment letter to undergo ongoing monitoring. The dossier must be accompanied by a Polish-style notarial certificate and apostille from the jurisdiction of the shareholder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company's paid-in capital is less than 10% of the first inbound capital injection and is disbursed via a third-party payment processor rather than through a six-charity SWIFT chain, creating ambiguity about the beneficial ownership of the invested funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a legalized foreign investment declaration (FID) submitted to the Ministry of Economy and Finance, a bank-signed foreign currency deposit certificate showing the remitter is the same as the shareholder, a signed board resolution authorizing the capital increase, a letter of voluntary non-U.S. transfer certificate from a certified public accountant, and an audited opening balance sheet proving the operational receipt of the funds into the capital escrow account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Revenue invoices are denominated in USD but the corresponding export proceeds are not settled in KRW within the 30-day statutory window, either because of an offsetting arrangement or a foreign receivables financing facility, which is considered a violation of the export proceeds surrender rules by the bank compliance officer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a formal exemption request under Article 22 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Decree, including a trade receivables aging schedule, a copy of the export insurance policy from Korea Trade Insurance Corporation (K-SURE), and a letter from the foreign buyer's bank confirming the deferred payment terms. Provide a Corporate Foreign Exchange Deal confirmation and a statement from the designated foreign exchange bank showing that the held amount is within the approved reinvestment framework, along with the company's internal treasury policy manual covering FX risk management.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For inbound capital injection, the funds must be routed via MT103 SWIFT wire directly to the capital escrow account of the Yuhan Hoesa at a designated foreign exchange bank. The wire must carry the correct foreign exchange purpose code under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, most appropriately 'FD-1' for acquisition of shares or capital investment by a non-resident, or 'FD-2' for acquisition of contribution certificates. The bank is required to verify the foreign investor's identity, the foreign investment claim (under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act), and the receipt of the funds. Once the capital is credited, the bank issues a certificate of foreign exchange purchase, and the company must register the investment with the Korean Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) within 30 days. The capital verification process for statutory purposes likewise involves the bank confirming that the remitting party is exactly the shareholder, and the payment purpose is exclusively an equity injection; no personal or third-party payments are accepted unless structured as a subordinated loan with prior approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the distribution of IVD diagnostic reagents are facilitated through the following rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct delivery-based trade settlement with pre-approved foreign beneficiaries, always referencing the relevant export/import contract and the harmonized system code 3002.12 for diagnostic reagents; (2) Commercial letters of credit (L/C) are used for high-value repeat orders from hospitals and clinical reference laboratories, where the issuing bank confirms the documents, especially the certificate of analysis and cold-chain temperature logs, with a maximum tenour of 90 days under documentary credit terms; (3) Documentary collections (D/P and D/A) are suitable for lower-value transfers or for markets with hard currency deficiency, but the foreign exchange bank will require the submission of the original transport documents and a proof of delivery receipt before releasing the proceeds. All outbound disbursements require the submission of a 'payment order to foreign country' under the designated purpose code, including 'S-3' for purchases of goods or 'T-1' for trade-related services. No cash or third-party reference payments are permitted, and any payment surcharge beyond the invoice amount triggers a manual review.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Short-dated outright forward contracts (deliverable KRW/USD) for a tenor up to 12 months, executed with the designated foreign exchange bank and backed by underlying export purchase orders or import purchase contracts

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on KRW are not permissible for domestic residents or entities settling in KRW under real demand principles; offshore NDF use is prohibited for hedging the Korean won; only onshore deliverable forwards are viable for the Yuhan Hoesa treasury

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) are permissible when they correspond to the conversion of an underlying external debt or trade finance facility, limited to a total notional amount below the KRW 30 billion reporting threshold unless prior regulatory approval is obtained from the Ministry of Economy and Finance

FX options or option strategies are permitted only to hedge genuine trade receivables, with the mandated filing of the foreign exchange forward, swap, or option position report through the bank's system to the Bank of Korea within three business days of execution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return on taxable income, incorporating statutory financial statements of the Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea via HomeTax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for 31 December year-end, file by 31 March of the following year. A one-month extension to 30 April is available where an external audit has been appointed and approved by the tax office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 20% non-filing negligence penalty on the unfiled tax amount (40% if made fraudulent), 10% understatement penalty on omitted or understated taxable income, and 0.03% per-day overdue surcharge capped at 9%; prolonged non-payment or non-filing triggers asset seizure and the National Tax Service may administratively close the business and place the entity on the national tax delinquent list. Korean law does not require an annual commercial registry renewal or provide a US-style strike-off for tax non-filing, but the court may judicially dissolve the company for cessation of business.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax surcharge return based on the corporate income tax assessed for the preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent municipal or provincial revenue bureau in the jurisdiction where the Yuhan Hoesa is registered via WETAX
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due concurrently with the corporate income tax return; for 31 December year-end, 31 March of the following year, or 30 April where the audited filing extension applies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Local tax negligence penalty of 20% for failure to file and 10% for underreporting, plus 0.03% daily overdue surcharge up to 9%; continuous non-payment may result in administrative seizure of bank accounts and company assets for enforced collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary general meeting of members for approval of annual financial statements and, where relevant, appointment or removal of directors and confirmation of auditors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not a government filing; held at the registered office and recorded in the minute book, with the minutes available for inspection and production to the Commercial Registration Court if required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for 31 December year-end, no later than 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct monetary penalty is imposed, but failure to hold the annual meeting invalidates financial statement adoption and dividend distribution, exposes directors to liability, and gives any member the right to apply to the court for an order convening the meeting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited financial statements and external audit report for companies exceeding the statutory audit thresholds under the Korean External Audit Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through DART and the National Tax Service where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The audit report must be presented to the ordinary general meeting before financial statement approval; mandated filers must submit the audited financial statements to the Financial Supervisory Service within 2 weeks after the general meeting and in any event no later than 30 April for calendar-year companies using the audited filing extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint or file an external auditor may result in designation of an auditor by the Financial Supervisory Commission, administrative fines, loss of favorable tax filing extensions, and regulatory citation; repeated non-compliance may trigger formal inspection and adverse solvency rating outcomes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: South Korean national Corporate Income Tax under CITA Article 55 is progressive: 10% on tax base up to KRW 200,000,000; 20% above KRW 200,000,000 up to KRW 20,000,000,000; 22% above KRW 20,000,000,000 up to KRW 300,000,000,000; and 24% above KRW 300,000,000,000. A 10% Local Corporate Income Tax surcharge is added to the national corporate tax, producing an aggregate top effective rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Available incentives for a Korean IVD reagent distribution entity include the Foreign Investment Promotion Act tax holidays for qualifying free-economic-zone investment, Restriction of Special Taxation Act R&D tax credits (30% general, up to 50% growth-stage), new medical device technology tax credits, and loss carryforward utilization. No patent box applies to wholesale distribution, so the effective rate will approximate the statutory progressive rate unless explicit qualifying credits are claimed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Tax Calculation Schedule, including the Foreign Corporation Annex, filed electronically through the National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax e-filing portal. The local corporate income tax surcharge is filed with the relevant local government but is computed in the same corporate tax return packet.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing with semi-annual estimated corporate tax prepayments during the fiscal year for corporations with a business year longer than six months.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return is due on the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, the statutory deadline is March 31 of the following calendar year. A qualifying foreign corporation may request a short extension through NTS administrative procedures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1a - Identifying Information and Foreign Corporation Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate name, business registration number, representative, head office address, Korean place of business, foreign shareholder schedule, and ultimate beneficial owner declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose whether the Korean Yuhan Hoesa is a domestic corporation or a foreign corporation under CITA Article 94. Identify every Korean permanent establishment and the foreign home-office branch relationship. Failure to declare a Korean PE in a distribution warehouse, local sales office, or dependent-agent sales force exposes the local entity to re-attribution of all Korean wholesale revenue to the PE and to branch withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5a - Gross Sales and Net Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross wholesale revenue from clinical diagnostic ELISA assays and IVD reagents, reduced by sales returns, trade discounts, rebates, and value-added tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all Korean-source gross revenue attributable to the Korean PE. Do not include direct cross-border sales by a foreign principal unless storage, inventory, or agent activity creates a PE in Korea. Intercompany purchasing from the foreign parent or related distributor must be recorded at arm's length; revenue misallocation between the foreign seller and the Korean distributor is a primary transfer pricing red flag for the NTS.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10a - Adjusted Tax Base and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Book net income reconciled to taxable income by adding non-deductible expenses, disallowed interest, excessive royalties, and fines, and by subtracting tax-exempt income, foreign-source dividend exemption, and net operating loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Korean NOL carryforward only within the 10-year statutory window. Head-office expense allocations must be supported by OECD-type allocation schedules and documentation; unsupported allocations will be treated as disguised profit transfers to the foreign head office. For a foreign-owned Korean distribution subsidiary, thin-capitalization interest disallowance applies when debt-to-equity from a controlling foreign shareholder exceeds 2:1.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 13a - Corporate Tax Computed and Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of national corporate tax at the 10%, 20%, 22%, and 24% brackets, plus the 10% Local Corporate Income Tax surcharge, and application of foreign tax credit, R&D tax credit, and prior-year credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits are available on foreign-source income that is legally and effectively attributable to the Korean PE, but the credit is limited to the Korean tax attributable to that foreign-source income. A treaty-shopping recipient without beneficial ownership should not claim treaty-derived credits. Documentary evidence of foreign tax payment and PE attribution must be retained for NTS examination.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 17a - Non-Resident Withholding Tax Schedule and Treaty Relief Statement
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of gross outbound dividends, interest, and royalties paid to foreign shareholders, foreign lenders, and foreign licensors, together with the withholding tax computed at the domestic rate or the claimed treaty rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute 20% national withholding tax plus the 2% local surcharge on each outbound payment unless a reduced treaty rate is substantiated before payment. Attach the NTS treaty relief application, foreign Tax Residency Certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, shareholding evidence for reduced dividend rates, and supporting contracts. If treaty relief is not approved before filing, the payer remains liable to remit the full 22%; a refund must be pursued through a rectification claim within the statutory assessment period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or late filing attracts an additional tax of 20% of the unpaid corporate tax; unfaithful underreporting attracts 10%; fraudulent underreporting attracts 40%; overdue payments incur a 0.022% daily late-payment surcharge. Criminal tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act Article 3 carries imprisonment up to 3 years or a fine up to 5 times the tax evaded, aggravated to 10 years for habitual evasion. The representative director may be jointly and severally liable for corporate tax liabilities when corporate assets are insufficient to satisfy the assessment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate on outbound dividends paid by a Korean corporation to a non-resident shareholder: 20% national Corporate Income Tax withholding under CITA plus 2% Local Corporate Income Tax surcharge. A DTA may reduce the rate, commonly to 10% for beneficial corporate shareholders owning at least 10% of voting capital and to 15% otherwise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before making the repatriation payment, the Korean payer must file the NTS Application for Tax Exemption/Reduction for Non-Resident or Foreign Corporation and attach: (i) a valid Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign recipient's competent tax authority within 12 months; (ii) a signed beneficial ownership declaration proving legal ownership, control, and economic entitlement to the income; (iii) for reduced dividend withholding, shareholder registers and constitutive documents proving continuous minimum voting ownership under the applicable DTA; (iv) for royalties and interest, the license or loan agreement and proof of arm's length rates; and (v) substance documentation of the foreign recipient, including office, employees, bank account, and board authority. If the treaty application is rejected, the payer must withhold the full 22%; a refund of excess withholding may be claimed through NTS rectification procedures.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for intellectual property and interest on intercompany debt paid to a non-resident without a Korean PE are subject to statutory withholding of 20% national tax plus 2% local surcharge, or 22% aggregate. Under many Korean bilateral DTAs the rate is reduced to 10% or 15% for interest and royalties, provided the recipient is the beneficial owner and, for royalties, the true legal and economic owner of the intangible asset. Disguised service fees embedded in royalty payments are not treaty-protected and will be recharacterized by the NTS as Korean-source taxable services.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Korean transfer pricing documentation thresholds under the Law for the Coordination of International Tax Affairs require a Local File when aggregate annual foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 50,000,000,000; a Master File when aggregate annual foreign related-party transactions exceed KRW 100,000,000,000; and a Country-by-Country Report when the multinational group's consolidated revenue is at least KRW 1,000,000,000,000. Even below these thresholds, contemporaneous OECD-compliant transfer pricing documentation is strongly advisable for a wholly foreign-owned Korean IVD reagent distribution entity.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate a zero-tax Economic Substance Regulations regime like the UAE, but economic substance doctrine is enforced through OECD BEPS standards, the Korean general anti-abuse rule, and treaty limitation-on-benefits and principal-purpose tests. The Korean Yuhan Hoesa must prove Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea: local distribution decisions, reagent inventory ownership and risk, qualified sales and regulatory personnel, independent board meetings, and the required IVD wholesale license. If the Korean entity is a registered shell with no commercial activity, no employees, no local decision-making, and no regulatory substance, NTS will disregard the entity, deny treaty benefits, and reattribute profits to the foreign shareholders.
